title: Latency ghosts in FlashPaged + fused ops — investigative notes
content:
Summary:

We see intermittent high tail-latency spikes (the "latency ghosts") in FlashPaged serving with fused ops enabled. Spikes are narrow (single-request level) and correlate with kernel-switch handoffs and occasional memory thrashing on SMs. Observed on both A100 and H100 clusters, more frequent at mid-to-high sequence lengths (1024–4096) and small batches (1–4).

Symptoms / metrics observed:
- Stable p50: ~3.1 ms per token for seq 2048 batch=1; p95: ~18–24 ms; p99: bursts up to 200–400 ms (single tokens).
- GPU SM utilization: jumps from 62% -> 98% during spike windows, then back down; NVLink and PCI traffic show short bursts of increased activity.
- Kernel timeline (tracebench): rapid kernel churn where prefetched fusion kernels are evicted/suspended and fallback kernels run for 1–3ms.
- KV cache size and reuse rate: small variance, but spikes sometimes follow a high-cache-miss micro-burst.

Where it differs from previous reports: this file focuses on the narrow, single-request spikes that we couldn't reproduce deterministically and which do not correlate with whole-host load or typical queueing phenomena documented earlier. Existing docs covered steady-state throughput and kernel fusion correctness; this is about transient stutters and why fused execution sometimes regresses.

Repro recipe (fastest path to see a ghost locally):
1) checkpoint: model="llama-3-8b" (quantized to q4f16), runtime binary: build/flashpaged/fusedops:latest-debug
2) hardware: single H100, 80GB, driver 535.xx, CUDA 12.2 (same as infra test rig)
3) bench command: 
   ./run_tracebench --model llama-3-8b --mode flashpaged --batch 1 --seq 2048 --prompt-set perf-tailset.json --iterations 200 --trace /tmp/trace.pb
4) env overrides used in experiments: 
   - RUNTIME_PREFETCH=1
   - FUSED_OPS=1
   - KVCACHE_ENABLED=1
   - PREFETCH_THREADS=4
   - KERNEL_SWITCH_COOLOFF_MS=0
5) Expected to hit a spike within 50–150 iterations on our trace set. If not reproducible, increase PREFETCH_THREADS to 8 or run multiple parallel clients.

Trace analysis highlights (examples from run #2024-11-20_01):
- Timeline excerpt (Timestamps are ms since bench start):
  [12034.2] request #87 enter scheduler
  [12034.3] kernel A (fusion-prefetch) start  - duration 0.8ms
  [12034.6] kernel B (flashpaged-attn) start - duration 0.9ms
  [12035.4] kernel A (fusion-prefetch) resumed? - additional 2.1ms
  [12037.0] fallback kernel C (non-fused attn) start - duration 18.3ms  <-- this is the ghost
  [12055.4] request #87 finish
- Flamegraph pattern: a short series of <1ms kernels followed by a single long kernel in a different cuda-stream. The long kernel is often the legacy non-fused attention kernel.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel preemption/hand-off bug: fused-prefetch kernel triggers a path that calls a different kernel variant, but state left on SMs requires a costly synchronization leading to fallback.
2) Memory placement thrash: prefetch writes a page and causes TLB misses or L2 misses that blow up latency for the next kernel invocation.
3) Small-race in scheduler: the kernel selection logic toggles between fused and non-fused kernels depending on micro-bench results, but the toggling can trigger a heavy-weight fallback if the cache state is unfavorable.
4) GPU driver/CUDA async scheduling edge-case: driver re-orders or serializes kernels when many tiny kernels are queued, leading to starvation that looks like a single long kernel.

Experiments run so far and outcomes:
A) Disable fused ops (FUSED_OPS=0): spikes disappear, p99 falls to ~45 ms. Indicates fused ops are involved.
B) Force single kernel stream (FORCE_SINGLE_STREAM=1): spike rate drops by ~60% but not eliminated. Suggests stream switching contributes.
C) Increase KERNEL_SWITCH_COOLOFF_MS to 5ms (keep using fused ops): spike frequency drops and duration reduces by ~50%. This mitigates the problem, consistent with scheduler-induced churn.
D) Turn off prefetch (RUNTIME_PREFETCH=0): spike frequency reduces slightly; some ghosts still occur. Points back to scheduler/kernel selection rather than prefetch writes alone.
E) Run on A100 vs H100: both reproduce but A100 shows slightly lower p99 max. Hardware affects magnitude but not root cause.

Low-level artifacts observed:
- Small allocations/free spikes in device malloc logs around ghost times.
- A few CUDA API warnings in the debug build (stream priority inversion on stream id 7) — needs follow-up.
- Trace samples show a high number of L2 cache misses during the long kernel windows (L2 miss ratio ~3x baseline).

Actions / next steps (near-term):
1) Instrument kernel selector to log decision inputs (sequence length, batch, kv-hit-rate, recent kernel latency history) and attach ID to traces. Owner: Evan. Target: 2024-11-22.
2) Add a lightweight per-stream backoff/hold timer to avoid immediate kernel toggling. Experiment: KERNEL_SWITCH_COOLOFF default to 2ms in canary. Owner: Jian. Target: 2024-11-28.
3) Capture full CUDA runtime API traces (cudaProf or Nsight with API) for a reproducer run to see driver-level reorders. Owner: Priya. Target: 2024-11-25.
4) Add microbench in kernel chooser: spin 5 warmup iterations and use median of last 3 kernel times instead of latest sample to avoid noisy micro-decisions. Owner: Marisol. Target: 2024-12-02.
5) Investigate whether small device malloc/free pattern is coming from fused ops code path; add pooling for ephemeral buffers. Owner: Marisol. Target: 2024-12-09.

Potential mitigations for canary rollout (if tests validate):
- Default kernel switch cooldown of 2–5 ms to reduce churn.
- Use stream affinity: bind certain request classes to a dedicated cuda-stream to avoid interleaving tiny kernels from different requests.
- Aggressive warmup: run 1–2 warmup fused kernels per model-load to stabilize kernel selection signals.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why does disabling fused ops remove spikes but not eliminate all p99 noise? Are there multiple independent causes?
- Is the fallback kernel really a single kernel or an aggregated effect of serialized tiny kernels from other requests?
- Are small device allocations causing fragmentation that increases kernel latency when allocations happen concurrent to kernel launches?

Logs and snippets (sanitized):
- scheduler.log excerpt: 
  2024-11-20T12:03:54.321Z [req=87] choose_kernel: fused_prefetch candidate_score=0.87 last_sample_ms=0.9 kv_hit=0.84
  2024-11-20T12:03:54.324Z [req=87] execute_kernel: stream=5 kernel_id=fused_prefetch
  2024-11-20T12:03:54.327Z [req=87] kernel_handoff: choose_kernel: nonfused_attn candidate_score=0.58 (fallback)
  2024-11-20T12:03:54.327Z [req=87] kernel_execute: nonfused_attn stream=7

- small flame excerpt (times in us): 
  fused_prefetch: 800 us
  flashpaged_attention: 900 us
  nonfused_attention: 18300 us  <-- ghost

Notes to self / heuristics brainstorm (quick):
- Kernel cooldown timer seems promising because we empirically reduced spike frequency in canary runs when we artificially increased it. But too-large cooldown will reduce adaptability and hurt throughput for mixed workloads.
- Favor median-based microbench smoothing to avoid reacting to single-sample noise.
- Pool ephemeral buffers in fused path to reduce device malloc churn.
- Add per-kernel L2 miss rate sampling (if cheap) to detect when memory placement is the culprit.

Decision log / tentative plan:
- Immediately: enable KERNEL_SWITCH_COOLOFF=2ms in nightly canary (small % of traffic) with detailed tracing enabled. If p99 reduces by >40% with <5% throughput regression, plan staged rollout.
- Medium-term: implement median smoothing and ephemeral buffer pooling; re-run full-scale tests on both A100/H100.

Owners and contact list:
- Priya Mehta (author): priya@redwood.ai - overall coordination, trace capture and analysis
- Evan Clarke: scheduler instrumentation and logs
- Marisol Gomez: fused-op path changes, buffer pooling
- Jian Wu: canary rollout and telemetry validation

Appendix: quick commands used / tooling
- Tracebench: ./run_tracebench --help (internal)
- Nsight capture: nsight-cu-cli --target-processes all --output /tmp/nsight_run.ncu ./run_tracebench ...
- Quick pprof: python -m pprof.traceview /tmp/trace.pb

If you reproduce locally, paste the first 10 lines of scheduler.log and the top-3 kernels from the flamegraph into this doc and ping the owners.
